Consulting
I take on selective consulting engagements in data science, machine learning, and quantitative analytics, drawing on prior industry experience across capital markets, financial services, and legal. Reach out via the email on my homepage if you would like to discuss a potential engagement.

title: Christy Coulson
text:
I am a Social Data Scientist and PhD Candidate at LSE in the Department of Methodology. My research sits at the intersection of interpretable machine learning, political methodology, and conflict studies. I’m particularly interested in how we can leverage the predictive fidelity of advanced ML while preserving the explanatory and inferential qualities of traditional parametric methods. Substantively, I work on protest dynamics, armed group strategy, and the determinants of inter- and intra-state conflict. I also teach and consult on applied data science, machine learning, and causal inference.
Before academia, I spent a few years as a derivatives trader and data scientist across capital markets, financial services, and legal, leading data science and AI transformation projects for both internal and client-facing work. I still take on selective consulting and enjoy thinking about how to translate methodological advances into actionable practice.

title: Research
text:
My methodological work sits at the intersection of interpretable machine learning and political methodology. I am interested in how we can leverage the predictive fidelity of advanced ML models while preserving the explanatory and inferential qualities of traditional parametric methods. In practice, this means asking what quantities from a fitted ML model can defensibly support causal, descriptive, or measurement claims — and under what conditions they cannot. Current work develops post-hoc measures for discovering candidate moderators of treatment effect heterogeneity, examines the interpretive limits of observation-level SHAP values in socially sensitive decision contexts, and adapts concept-based interpretability methods to audit the construct validity of political text classifiers.
Substantively, I work on conflict, protest, and political violence. My interests span the strategic behaviour of armed groups, the dynamics linking protest to subsequent political violence, and the legislative and judicial responses to contentious politics. I am particularly drawn to questions where the underlying data-generating process is complex enough that standard parametric models under-perform, but where the inferential stakes require more than black-box prediction.
